description: Plays one MPX part on a modelled violin: four strings bowed through a model of rosin's friction, on one bridge and one body, each note's bowing chosen by a model of a player.

params.name: Vibrato
params.text: How wide the vibrato is, as a share of each note's own width: at the middle, each note's own — wider on long and loud notes, none on open strings or where the part says senza vibrato, narrower in earlier music; at the bottom, none; at the top, twice as wide. A change is heard at once, on the notes already sounding.

params.name: Brightness
params.text: Turns the violin's highs down. Fully clockwise, the violin as it is; turned counter-clockwise, everything above about 2.5 kHz is turned down, by up to 12 dB fully counter-clockwise, and nothing below it is touched. A filter on the output, after the violin: it changes nothing about how the notes are bowed or started.

params.name: Record
params.text: Records what the module puts out to a WAV file while it is lit, with a text file beside it listing every note: how it began, the bow's force, speed and place, and whether its start was tried ahead. In the Rack user folder, under DreamerMPX/recordings; the right-click menu opens the folder. Each file is named for the module, the time, and how far into the piece it began.

inputs.name: MPX note
inputs.text: One part, played on the violin: its notes, from mpxScore or any MPX source. From a score each note is announced ahead, and at Fidelity levels 1 to 3 its start is worked out before it sounds.

inputs.name: Gate
inputs.text: Plays the violin without a cable: a note while the gate is up, let go when it falls. With a polyphonic gate, the highest pitch among the channels that are up. Each note is played as it comes, as Fidelity's live level plays it, since nothing says ahead what is coming. While an MPX cable is in, this port and the three below it are not read.

inputs.name: 1V/oct
inputs.text: The pitch of the gate's note, a volt an octave, nought at middle C. A move of more than half a semitone while the gate stays up is the next note, slurred in the same bow; a smaller one is left alone.

inputs.name: Level
inputs.text: How loud each gate's note is played, read as it begins: nought volts ppp, ten fff, in sevenths between. With nothing patched, mf.

inputs.name: Vibrato CV
inputs.text: Added to the VIB knob: five volts add as much as the knob's middle, and the sum is held between none and twice each note's own width.

outputs.name: Out
outputs.text: The violin, in mono, as loud as mpxPiano playing the same markings. A single note at fff peaks about 2.5V.

lights.name: Level
lights.text: Flashes green as each note begins, lights orange when the output passes 7.07V, 3 dB under clipping, and red when it reaches 10V, where Rack's audio interface clips.

notes: From a score, each note is announced to the module four and a half seconds before it sounds. At Fidelity levels 1 to 3, ways of starting it are tried on a copy of the violin while the music plays. A note from a keyboard or a generator, which nothing announced, is played as it arrives.
One violin plays one note at a time: a chord on the cable is played as its top note, and of the channels of a polyphonic gate, the highest whose gate is up. A section is a module for each player.

A part on the cable that goes below the violin's lowest open string is played as a whole an octave or two higher, as far as its highest note allows, and one that goes past the end of the fingerboard, two octaves and a sixth above the highest string, an octave or two lower. Any note still out of reach, and any from the ports, is moved by octaves by itself. While the part goes out of reach, the plug light on the source's output blinks. Notes high on the fingerboard but within it are played where they are written.

Fidelity, in the right-click menu, sets how much is tried on a copy of the violin before each note sounds. Level 1 tries up to eighteen ways of starting each note from the string, and each bow change three ways. Level 2 tries two ways of starting, a short glide and one bite. Level 3 plays one bite without trying it and still tries each bow change. Level 4, the default, tries nothing: each note is played as it arrives, so notes need not be announced ahead, and no second copy of the violin is worked out, for the least computing.

Enable diagnostics, in the right-click menu, shows the number and the REC button along the top of the panel; it is on to begin with. The number counts the notes announced on the cable that were played without anything tried, because the trying had not finished when they were due; a busy computer is the usual cause. Notes nobody announced, from a keyboard or the ports, are not counted. It counts from nought whenever Fidelity, Economy or the part's range changes and whenever the source goes back to its start, and stays at nought at level 4.

Economy, in the right-click menu, is for less computing at less fidelity: the strings are worked out at half the rate, and a string nobody is playing stops once it has rung down, so it no longer rings in sympathy with the others. It takes about half the computing.
